Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this. We're running through a SOC 2 readiness checklist and the auditors have asked for a clear description and sample exports of admin/event logging for the past 90 days. High-level asks:

- What admin events are logged (user management, role changes, API key operations, model deployment/rollback, dedicated node changes, etc.)?
- Retention default windows for admin logs and privileged actions; how do retention and legal holds interact?
- Preferred export formats you can produce (JSONL, Parquet, CSV) and whether you can produce a signed manifest with per-file checksums and HMAC.
- Timezone normalization (are timestamps UTC by default?) and any timezone fields included.
- Redaction options for PII (can you replace emails/IDs with deterministic hashing or provide mapping under NDA?).
- Delivery options: S3 presigned + manifest, SFTP, or drive links.

I've attached: SIG-v3-questions.xlsx and Greenleaf_Audit_Request.pdf for context. Ideally we get a sample extract and manifest today if possible; otherwise earliest tomorrow morning PT.

Thanks,
Oliver Chan
Head of Compliance
Greenleaf Health

Thanks Oliver — happy to help. Short answer up front and then a sample plan below.

Quick summary (we can hand off a packaged bundle with checksums and a signed manifest):
- Logged event surface: account admin actions (create/delete user, role grants/revokes), API key lifecycle (create/rotate/revoke), model deploy/rollback events (model_id, version, config changes), infra ops (node allocation, pool resize, dedicated scaling), console/admin-console logins (success/fail), permission changes, and operator impersonation events.
- Timestamps: all events are stored with RFC3339 timestamps in UTC by default (both event_ts and ingest_ts). We also preserve the source timezone in a separate field when available.
- Retention: default 365 days for privileged/admin events; 90 days for general operational audit logs. Legal hold: we support per-tenant hold that suspends TTL expiration and flags exports.
- Export formats: JSONL (primary), Parquet (columnar), and compressed tar.gz bundles. We provide an HMAC-SHA256-signed manifest per bundle and SHA256 checksums per file.
- Delivery: S3 (pre-signed PUT or cross-account role), SFTP, and secure Drive links (for low-volume). We can also push to your S3 if you provide a role ARN.
- Redaction: deterministic hashing for emails/IDs (HMAC-based) or full redaction; mapping file delivered under NDA if required.

Proposed sample bundle (what we can produce today):
- 90-day JSONL sample (admin-events-sample.jsonl) compressed and SHA256ed.
- manifest.json (bundle-level metadata + HMAC signature)
- checksum.txt (per-file SHA256)
- readme.txt (field schema + export timestamp + timezone normalization note)

Next steps: 1) confirm preferred delivery method (S3 with ARN, or we provide presigned URL), 2) confirm if you want deterministic hashing mapping or redaction-only, 3) confirm retention/hold rules as you'd like them documented for SOC 2 evidence.

Looping in Kim and Naomi for the manifest and packaging details.

— Vivek

On Wed, Dec 30, 2026 at 11:02 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Oliver — happy to help. Short answer up front and then a sample plan below.

Adding export manifest and schema details so your auditors can validate automatically.

Field set we include in JSONL (one object per line):
- event_ts: RFC3339 UTC timestamp (string)
- ingest_ts: RFC3339 UTC timestamp (string)
- tenant_id: tenant identifier (hashed if requested)
- actor_email: email of caller (hashed/redacted on request)
- actor_id: internal user id (GUID)
- action: canonical action string (e.g., USER_CREATE, APIKEY_ROTATE, MODEL_DEPLOY)
- resource_type: e.g., user, api_key, model, infra_node
- resource_id: resource identifier (hashed optional)
- ip_address: client ip (anonymized to /24 on request)
- request_id: opaque request id for traceability
- trace_id: optional distributed trace id if available
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- change_summary: short human-readable delta or ACL diff (we redact tokens)
- raw_payload_ref: pointer to attached payload in bundle (if any)

Packaging & integrity:
- File naming: <tenant>-admin-events-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.jsonl.gz
- Per-file SHA256 recorded in checksum.txt
- manifest.json includes: bundle_id, files:[{name,size,sha256}], export_window:{from,to}, timezone:UTC, exporter:vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
- Manifest signed with HMAC-SHA256 using a key we can provision temporarily; auditors can verify signature.

Retention and legal hold notes:
- By default we will not delete data under an active legal hold; holds are tenant-scoped and require explicit release from the customer legal contact.
- Snapshots for audits are immutable once the manifest is signed; we keep a copy (attestation) for 30 days after delivery for repro/verification.

Redaction options (pick one):
1) Deterministic HMAC hash of emails/IDs (audit mapping made available under NDA)
2) Full redaction (replaced with <REDACTED>)
3) Pseudonymization + mapping file accessible via encrypted transfer

If you confirm option 1 or 3, we will need an NDA/DP agreement for the mapping file transfer (DocuSign link OK).

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Security Manager
